mcqs.q: In the Onomichi community-cat health survey, what proportion of cats tested FIV-positive by ELISA?
mcqs.e: ELISA showed 16.7% of the community cats were FIV-positive.

mcqs.q: What was the detected carriage rate of Capnocytophaga, a zoonotic risk to tourists/residents?
mcqs.e: All sampled cats (100%) carried Capnocytophaga, with Bartonella henselae at 38%.

mcqs.q: What did the authors recommend for friendly cats given their findings?
o: Maintain them long-term as community cats
Adopt them out rather than keep them as community cats
mcqs.e: They recommended friendly cats be adopted rather than maintained as community cats, and a CCP review.

mcqs.q: What did the population-dynamics data conclude about the CCP 'closed, static colony' hypothesis?
o: It was rejected due to immigration of non-neutered cats
It was supported with minor caveats
mcqs.e: Thirteen non-neutered cats immigrated within a year, rejecting the closed-population hypothesis.

mcqs.q: How many non-neutered cats immigrated into the CCP area within a year?
mcqs.e: Thirteen non-neutered cats immigrated, indicating rapid turnover.

mcqs.q: What was the study's overall verdict on CCP efficacy?
o: Limited efficacy with rapid turnover; neither restricts breeding nor improves welfare
mcqs.e: The CCP showed limited efficacy and could not support lifetime management due to turnover.

mcqs.q: In the Brazilian survey, allowing cats outdoor access was associated with:
o: Higher odds of welfare problems (e.g., sporotrichosis, going missing, accidents)
mcqs.e: Outdoor access carried significantly higher odds of fleas, sporotrichosis, going missing, poisoning, mistreatment, and accidents.

mcqs.q: What proportion of respondents reported allowing their cats outdoor access?
mcqs.e: 37.1% of respondents allowed outdoor access.

mcqs.q: Which factor was significantly associated with allowing outdoor access?
mcqs.e: Unneutered status and rural residence (plus younger owner age) were among the associated factors.

mcqs.q: What did the 598-cat Danish necropsy study conclude about the belief that unsocialised cats suffer a high welfare burden?
o: Welfare problems were only moderate; most had no major finding
mcqs.e: Over 83% had no major finding and 54% none at all, indicating only a moderate welfare problem level.

mcqs.q: What percentage of the cats were emaciated?
mcqs.e: Only 0.3% were emaciated; >83% had normal body condition.

mcqs.q: What was the most common finding on necropsy?
mcqs.e: Ectoparasites were most common (lice 15.9%, fleas 12.3%); FeLV was only 1.2%.

mcqs.q: How does the review characterize the sociality of free-ranging cats?
mcqs.e: Findings support free-ranging cats as social generalists displaying flexible social behavior.

mcqs.q: How did intraspecific social dynamics compare across cat groups?
o: Variable—some strongly bonded, others loosely associated
mcqs.e: Dynamics differed by group, from strong affiliations to little interaction.

mcqs.q: Free-ranging cats' interactions with wildlife were most strongly linked to:
mcqs.e: Wildlife interactions were strongly tied to the timing of cat feeding events.

mcqs.q: What core gap did the review identify in New Zealand cat management?
o: Lack of national legislation, causing inconsistent practices
mcqs.e: Absence of national cat legislation challenges consistent, humane, effective management.

mcqs.q: What solution did the authors ultimately propose?
mcqs.e: They offered a solution based on national cat legislation.

mcqs.q: Which country was emphasized for policy comparison with New Zealand?
mcqs.e: The review compared NZ's policy landscape with other countries, emphasizing Australia.

mcqs.q: What relationship between human density and dog numbers did the Chile analysis find?
o: More dogs per person as density rises
Fewer dogs per person as human density increases
mcqs.e: As human density increased, there were fewer dogs per person.

mcqs.q: What did the authors recommend regarding free veterinary services?
o: Replace free vet services with low-cost sterilization campaigns
mcqs.e: They recommended replacing free vet services with low-cost sterilization campaigns.

mcqs.q: Which component was notably absent from Chile's program?
mcqs.e: Enforcement was not included; the authors recommended creating enforcement teams.

mcqs.q: What was the estimated national population of unowned free-ranging cats in Denmark?
mcqs.e: The estimate was 89,000 ± 11,000 cats, density ~2/km2.

mcqs.q: In which habitat did these cats primarily live?
mcqs.e: The cats lived primarily in rural habitats.

mcqs.q: What was the estimated socialisation split of the population?
mcqs.e: Roughly one-third were socialised and two-thirds unsocialised.

mcqs.q: During the breeding season on the Chinese campus, how did male and female home ranges compare?
mcqs.e: Males had larger breeding-season home ranges (12.60 ha) than females (5.02 ha).

mcqs.q: When did the cats' two daily activity peaks occur?
mcqs.e: Activity peaked 6:00–10:00 and 17:00–21:00, i.e., crepuscular/twilight.

mcqs.q: Home range size of these free-ranging cats was affected by:
mcqs.e: Home range was affected by breeding status and sex.

mcqs.q: How did neuter status affect roaming in male companion cats?
o: Intact males spent more time away and had larger home ranges
mcqs.e: Intact males spent more time away and had larger home ranges than neutered males.

mcqs.q: What effect did heavy rainfall have on distance moved?
mcqs.e: On heavy-rain days cats moved ~2.4 km vs ~3.6 km on dry days.

mcqs.q: Compared with younger cats, cats over seven years old were:
o: Less active with smaller home ranges
mcqs.e: Older cats spent less time away, were less active, and had smaller home ranges.

mcqs.q: Under the 25-year Auckland Trap–Assess–Resolve (TAR) program, what was the primary outcome for trapped cats?
o: Most returned to site via TNR
mcqs.e: Of 14,611 cats, 64.2% were adopted, with adoption rates exceeding 80% by 2018–19.

mcqs.q: TAR is presented as a third management strategy, an alternative to:
mcqs.e: TAR is framed as an alternative to the usual choice between culling and TNR.

mcqs.q: What was the age profile of the trapped cats?
o: About 52% were young kittens under 10 weeks
mcqs.e: Consistently ~52% were kittens <10 weeks and ~80% were under 1 year old.

mcqs.q: In the Prince George survey, support for free-roaming cat bylaws differed mainly by:
mcqs.e: Perceptions and bylaw support depended on cat-ownership status, with non-owners more supportive.

mcqs.q: What concern did cat owners raise about restrictive roaming bylaws?
mcqs.e: Owners feared such bylaws would increase abandonment and harm pet care.

mcqs.q: There was considerable public support for which measure?
mcqs.e: There was considerable support for mandatory identification of cats.
